title: Imperfect pouvoir
subtitle: Saying could / was able to
explanation: Use the imperfect forms of pouvoir to talk about what someone could do or was able to do in the past.

title: Imperfect vouloir
subtitle: Saying wanted / was wanting
explanation: Use voulais, voulions, vouliez, and voulaient to talk about what people wanted in the past.

examples.eng: What did you want to do yesterday?

title: Dire à
subtitle: Telling something to someone
explanation: Use dire for “to say / to tell”. When you name the person receiving the information, the course uses dire à + person.

examples.fre: j'ai besoin de dire à Marie

examples.eng: I'm going to tell Pierre everything tomorrow.
examples.fre: Je vais tout dire à Pierre demain.

title: Imperfect devoir
subtitle: Saying had to / was supposed to
explanation: Use the imperfect of devoir to say what someone had to do in the past.

examples.eng: What did you have to do?
examples.fre: Que devais-tu faire? / Que deviez-vous faire?

title: Garer and se garer
subtitle: Parking something vs parking yourself
explanation: Use garer when you park a vehicle or other object. Use se garer when the person is parking or finding a place to park.

examples.eng: I park / I am parking myself

examples.fre: Puis-je me garer quelque part ici?

title: Quelque part
subtitle: Saying somewhere
explanation: Use quelque part for “somewhere”. It can be used with location, movement, and parking questions.

examples.fre: Il est quelque part en France.

examples.eng: Is there somewhere where I can park nearby?
examples.fre: Y a-t-il quelque part où je peux me garer près d'ici?

title: Quelqu'un
subtitle: Someone / somebody / anyone
explanation: Use quelqu’un for someone or somebody. In questions, the same expression can also match “anyone / anybody”.

examples.eng: Did you see somebody at the hotel?
examples.fre: As-tu / Avez-vous vu quelqu'un à l'hôtel?

title: Quelquefois
subtitle: Saying sometimes
explanation: Use quelquefois for “sometimes” when an action or situation happens on some occasions.

examples.eng: Sometimes I go to France, but sometimes I go to Spain.
examples.fre: Quelquefois je vais en France, mais quelquefois je vais en Espagne.

examples.eng: Sometimes, it's very cold in London.
examples.fre: Quelquefois, il fait très froid à Londres.

title: Imperfect savoir
subtitle: Saying knew
explanation: Use the imperfect of savoir to talk about what someone knew in the past.

examples.eng: We knew where it was but we were very tired.
examples.fre: Nous savions où c'était mais nous étions très fatigués.

title: Savoir + infinitive
subtitle: Knowing how to do something
explanation: The course uses savoir followed directly by an infinitive for knowing how to do an activity.

examples.eng: I know how to ride horses

title: Que, ce que, and quoi
subtitle: Different ways to express what
explanation: Use que at the start of many questions, ce que inside a sentence for “what”, and quoi before an infinitive in patterns such as quoi faire.

examples.eng: I don't understand what you said.
examples.fre: Je ne comprends pas ce que tu as / vous avez dit.

examples.eng: Can you tell Jeanne what everybody wants to eat?
examples.fre: Peux-tu / Pouvez-vous dire à Jeanne ce que tout le monde veut manger?

examples.eng: I don't know what to do
examples.fre: je ne sais pas quoi faire

title: Reflexive pronouns
subtitle: Me, te, se, nous, vous
explanation: Reflexive verbs change the pronoun with the subject: me, te, se, nous, or vous. The pronoun stays with the verb or infinitive.

examples.eng: I park / I am parking myself
we park / we are parking ourselves

title: S'appeler
subtitle: Saying what someone is called
explanation: S’appeler is a reflexive verb used for names. The reflexive pronoun changes with the person.

title: Se laver and se lever
subtitle: Everyday reflexive actions
explanation: Use se laver for washing yourself and se lever for getting up. The reflexive pronoun changes with the subject.

title: Se rendre compte que
subtitle: Saying realise that
explanation: Use se rendre compte to say “to realise”. Add que before the thing you realise.

examples.fre: je me rends compte que Pierre ne vient pas
je me rends compte qu'il est tard

title: Faire: present and past
subtitle: Doing and making
explanation: Faire means “to do” or “to make”. In the passé composé, it uses avoir + fait.

title: Faire + infinitive
subtitle: Having or getting something done
explanation: The course uses faire + infinitive to show that someone causes another action to happen, such as getting a car washed or a house cleaned.

examples.eng: to have / to get + noun + past participle
I want to get the car washed tomorrow
examples.fre: Je veux faire laver la voiture demain

examples.eng: When can you get the house cleaned?
examples.fre: Quand peux-tu faire nettoyer la maison? / Quand pouvez-vous faire nettoyer la maison?

title: Faire expressions
subtitle: Cooking, shopping, and packing
explanation: Several common activities use faire: faire la cuisine, faire les courses, and faire ses valises.

title: Possessive adjectives
subtitle: My, your, his/her, our, their
explanation: Possessive words change to match the French noun. Course 11 practises forms such as son/sa/ses, notre/nos, and leur/leurs inside the packing examples.

title: Faire savoir
subtitle: Letting someone know
explanation: Use faire savoir to mean “to let someone know”. The person can be shown with a pronoun or with à + person.

examples.fre: je dois faire savoir à Pierre

examples.eng: Are you going to let me know?
Can you let everybody know what time we're having dinner?
examples.fre: Peux-tu / Pouvez-vous faire savoir à tout le monde à quelle heure nous prenons le dîner?

title: Imperfect être
subtitle: Saying was / were
explanation: Use étais, était, étions, étiez, and étaient to describe where or how people were in the past.

title: Il y a + past time
subtitle: Saying how long ago
explanation: Use il y a before a length of time to say “ago”. Course 11 also uses huit jours for a week and quinze jours for a fortnight.

examples.fre: il y a exactement un an
il y a exactement huit jours

title: Déjà
subtitle: Already and before
explanation: Déjà can mean “already”. In positive questions it can also match the idea of having done something before.

title: Toujours
subtitle: Saying still
explanation: Use toujours for “still” when a situation continues.

examples.fre: Tout le monde est toujours ici.

title: Pas encore
subtitle: Saying not yet
explanation: Use pas encore for “not yet”. In many sentences it surrounds the verb with ne ... pas encore.

examples.fre: Je n'ai pas encore vu Pierre.

title: Encore
subtitle: Again and another
explanation: Encore can mean “again”. Before a noun or quantity, it can also mean “another” or “more”.

examples.eng: I would like another bottle of wine
examples.fre: je voudrais encore une bouteille de vin

title: D'habitude
subtitle: Saying usually
explanation: Use d’habitude for “usually”. It can appear at the beginning or later in a sentence.

examples.eng: Where do you usually spend the holidays?
examples.fre: Où passes-tu les vacances d'habitude? / Où passez-vous les vacances d'habitude?

title: Peut-être que / inversion
subtitle: Saying maybe or perhaps
explanation: Peut-être can introduce “maybe / perhaps”. Course 11 shows both peut-être que + normal word order and a more formal inversion pattern.

examples.fre: Peut-être que nous pouvons aller plus tard. / Peut-être pouvons-nous aller plus tard.
Peut-être que Pierre est ici. / Peut-être Pierre est-il ici.

title: Envoyer + pronouns
subtitle: Sending something to someone
explanation: Envoyer means “to send”. Pronouns such as me, te/vous, and nous can stay before the infinitive or conjugated verb.

examples.eng: Can you send me an email?

title: Sending by post or email
subtitle: Par courrier, par email, par la poste
explanation: Use par to say how something is sent. Course 11 uses par courrier, par email / courrier électronique, and par la poste, and also mettre au courrier for putting something in the post.

examples.eng: I can send it by email.
examples.fre: Je peux l'envoyer par email / par courrier électronique.

title: Regions and directions
subtitle: North, south, east, west, and centre
explanation: Course 11 uses dans le nord/sud/est/ouest or dans le centre to locate places, and de/à with these region expressions when the sentence requires it.

examples.eng: I live in the north of England.
examples.fre: J'habite dans le nord de l'Angleterre.

examples.eng: Marseille is in the south of France.
examples.fre: Marseille est dans le sud de la France.

examples.eng: The west and east of France are very different.
examples.fre: L'ouest et l'est de la France sont très différents.
